title: Policy-as-code adaptive remediator with simulated drift runner and automated evidence packager
creator: Liam Patel
description: Background: We frequently detect configuration drift for data residency and retention controls between declared policy (policy-as-code) and live tenant configurations. Current remediation requires manual triage and ad-hoc evidence collection for audits. This ticket implements an adaptive remediation service that (1) runs controlled noisy-drift simulations to validate detection logic, (2) executes configurable remediation actions (dry-run / staged / auto-apply), and (3) produces tamper-evident evidence bundles for audit and reporting.
motivation: Reduce time to remediate compliance drifts, increase confidence in automatic fixes by validating against simulated drift scenarios, and standardize evidence export so SOC/compliance teams get consistent, encrypted bundles for audits.
design_summary: New microservice: policy-adaptive-remediator. Components: policy-evaluator (consumes policy-as-code catalog), drift-simulator (replay-and-inject synthetic misconfigs), remediation-orchestrator (dry-run / staged / auto modes), evidence-packager (signed JSON bundles with change diffs, request/response logs, timestamps), and a trust layer (ledger + KMS envelope). Integration points: config registry, tenant-metadata service, audit-log store, and console for rollouts. Feature flagging + canary per-tenant. All artifacts encrypted at rest via KMS and access-audited.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: 1) Auto-apply vs manual: default start is dry-run; schedule progressive canary to auto-apply for low-risk drifts. 2) Evidence storage: S3 encrypted with KMS chosen for scalability; ledger entries stored in existing compliance-ev DB for quick queries. 3) Remediation granularity: prefer config patch + idempotent ops; avoid full-config overwrite to reduce blast radius. 4) Drift simulation frequency: daily synthetic injections in staging and weekly in a shadowed subset of production tenants to validate detectors without impacting customers.
acceptance_criteria: Policy evaluator can ingest policy-as-code catalog and compute a deterministic set of assertions for residency and retention
Drift simulator can inject at least five synthetic drift patterns (region mislabel, retention too-long, retention-disabled, encryption-disabled, export-enabled) and emit results to telemetry
Remediation orchestrator supports dry-run, staged-apply (canary by tenant group), and auto-apply modes with audit logs for every action
Evidence packager produces signed, KMS-encrypted bundles with metadata and diffs; bundles retrievable via console and downloadable by compliance users for >90 days
End-to-end test harness simulates a drift, runs remediation in dry-run, and produces an evidence bundle that passes schema validation
Operational metrics: detection latency, remediation lead time, remediation success rate, false-positive rate and evidence bundle generation latency are emitted to the compliance dashboard
tasks: Spec: finalize policy-evaluator input/output schema and policy assertion language (use existing policy schema where possible)
Implement drift-simulator library and a small runner service for injecting synthetic drifts in staging
Build remediation-orchestrator service with safe-exec primitives and circuit-breakers
Implement evidence-packager: bundle format, signing, KMS envelope, storage path, retention policy
Integrate with telemetry: metrics + logs + traces and a compliance dashboard panel
Create canary plan and feature-flag controls in console for progressive rollout
Write end-to-end tests and CI jobs; include schema validation for evidence bundles
Security review and threat model for remediation roles and keys
Run a 2-week shadow run against 3 low-risk tenants and iterate on false-positive tuning
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): deploy simulator + evaluator, run 3 synthetic scenarios; Phase 2 (shadow prod): enable evaluator and evidence-packager in read-only mode against 3 pilot tenants for 2 weeks; Phase 3 (canary apply): enable staged-apply for pilot tenants with manual approval gating; Phase 4 (wider rollout): enable auto-apply for low-risk classes after 4 weeks of stable metrics. Rollback via feature flag. All phases require security sign-off.
monitoring_and_metrics: Emit metrics to compliance-prom: compliance.drift.detected, compliance.drift.simulated, compliance.remediation.attempted, compliance.remediation.success, evidence.bundle.created, evidence.bundle.size_bytes, compliance.false_positive_rate. Alert if remediation.success < 95% for two consecutive days or false_positive_rate > 3%.
runbook_summary: On remediation failure: revert using idempotent reverse-patch; escalate to on-call compliance lead. For evidence packager failures: queue bundle for retry and raise high-priority alert. For KMS errors: fail safe to dry-run and notify security team.
open_questions: What level of tenant consent is required before running synthetic drift injections in shadow production?
Should evidence bundles be globally retained 180 days by default or tenant-controlled retention?
Do we need a dedicated signing key (HSM-backed) for evidence bundles distinct from existing KMS keys?
What SLA do downstream auditors expect for evidence retrieval (minutes vs hours)?
